automation_name: AI Dev Wiki Topic News Collector

cutoff_window.rule: Include only public sources with visible publication or update dates inside the two-day window. Exclude future-dated, missing-date, ambiguous-date, or boundary-only candidates.

federation_boundary.local_scope: AI-assisted development practice: context architecture, guidance structure, agent operating practices, workflows, verification, governance, and local adoption patterns.
federation_boundary.upstream_owned_scope: The upstream AI wiki owns broad companies, models, products, developer tools, agentic frameworks, MCP servers, and techniques.
federation_boundary.collector_action: Record upstream-owned entities by name, but keep only local practice implications or routing notes in this raw artifact.

qualifying_updates.title: Governed-agent framework treats gateways as a runtime control plane
qualifying_updates.summary: LangChain describes governed agents as systems whose model calls, tool calls, MCP calls, and agent-to-agent hops need cost, permission, data-boundary, and trace controls at runtime.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: The local governance pages should keep treating agent governance as cross-cutting runtime control rather than only prompt policy or post-hoc observability.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Model routing, spend limits, PII redaction, tool permissions, MCP boundary checks, and per-hop tracing should be designed together as governed-agent runtime requirements.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Ingest as a governance-control pattern, not as a LangChain product leaf.

qualifying_updates.title: IssueBench evaluates trace issue detection, grouping, and repair
qualifying_updates.summary: LangChain describes an internal IssueBench benchmark for evaluating whether an agent-monitoring system can identify known issues in traces, assign failure categories, attach them to existing issues, and group new failures.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: It is a concrete eval pattern for agent operations: evaluate the issue-detection and clustering workflow itself, not just final answer quality.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Agent observability evals should include ground-truth trace defects, failure-category assignment, duplicate attachment, and issue clustering quality.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Possible ingest target: code-review evals, trajectory-level evals, or user-visible runtime telemetry.

qualifying_updates.title: GitHub Code Quality GA combines deterministic analysis with AI-assisted detection
qualifying_updates.summary: GitHub Code Quality became generally available with CodeQL-based maintainability and reliability analysis, AI-assisted detection, Copilot Autofix suggestions, organization dashboards, pull-request coverage metrics, ruleset gates, APIs, and paid usage.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: AI-assisted review is moving into enforceable pull-request gates and budgeted quality programs rather than only advisory review comments.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Teams adopting AI review should separate deterministic checks, AI-generated findings, AI-generated fixes, ruleset enforcement, and metered cost in their operating model.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Route broad GitHub product coverage upstream; keep local note to lifecycle review gates and cost governance.

qualifying_updates.title: AWS highlights one-click setup prompts that install serverless agent skills and MCP
qualifying_updates.summary: AWS describes a Lambda setup prompt for coding agents that configures serverless skills and the Serverless MCP server, with setup paths for several coding agents and a separate Agent Toolkit setup for current AWS knowledge and safe resource access.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Setup prompts are becoming operational artifacts that bootstrap agent skills, tool access, and service-specific best practices in one repeatable package.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Agent setup artifacts should be source-controlled, reviewable, dated, scoped to a service boundary, and paired with permission guidance for the tools they install.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Keep local treatment to setup-prompt governance and skill/tool bootstrap practice.

qualifying_updates.title: Community thread asks for AGENTS.md-style guidance around containerized operations
qualifying_updates.summary: A NethServer community thread argues that AI agents working inside NS8 modules need structured guidance similar to AGENTS.md, especially where container boundaries, host commands, log analysis, service restarts, and framework-specific commands differ from standard Docker assumptions.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: It is a practice-level example of durable instructions reducing repeated rediscovery and wrong-environment assumptions for coding and ops agents.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Durable agent instructions should encode runtime boundaries, approved operational commands, and environment-specific exceptions instead of relying on agents to infer them from generic documentation.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Possible ingest target: durable-instructions, instruction hierarchy, or request package boundaries.

qualifying_updates.title: OpenAI community discussion frames Codex context continuity as architecture plus retrieval
qualifying_updates.summary: A Codex forum thread asks how to preserve project context across sessions with AGENTS.md, skills, MCP, RAG, code graphs, and session summaries; replies distinguish architecture-driven context reduction from AST or graph-based retrieval for cross-service changes.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: It reinforces that context architecture is partly software architecture, partly durable instruction, and partly selective retrieval.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Long-lived codebase support should define stable architectural boundaries and use graph or retrieval layers only for the cross-boundary context that static instructions cannot safely preserve.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Potentially useful for context-state rehydration and code retrieval evidence patterns.

qualifying_updates.title: Agent protocol explainer separates tool access from agent delegation
qualifying_updates.summary: HowAIWorks maps MCP to agent-tool interaction, A2A to agent-agent delegation, and ACP to a historical agent-agent layer that folded into A2A.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Local MCP practice pages should avoid treating agent protocols as interchangeable; each layer carries different security, identity, and governance responsibilities.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Governance rules should distinguish tool-call approval, data-resource access, delegated-agent identity, and cross-organization trust boundaries.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Ingest as a local protocol-boundary practice note only if upstream does not already cover the broad protocol facts.

qualifying_updates.title: Agent-loop article argues the loop, not the model call, owns reliability
qualifying_updates.summary: Agentic Thinking argues that durable agent progress comes from loop design: termination, memory, recursion controls, fresh-context evaluation, external checks, and budgets around repeated model steps.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: The local agent-workflow and verification pages can use this as a practice signal for treating loop termination and external verification as first-class design surfaces.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Loop designs should define what stops the work, what persists across iterations, how fresh-context verifiers participate, and how recursion is bounded.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Avoid duplicating general technique history; keep local note to orient-inspect-patch-verify and verification-loop pages.

qualifying_updates.title: Agent-loop field guide catalogs bounded, conditional, check, fan-out, and nested loops
qualifying_updates.summary: A companion Agentic Thinking field guide describes loop shapes and axes such as control flow, stop conditions, memory, and who checks the result.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: This maps directly to local workflow design: planning loops, TDD loops, subagent fan-out, repair loops, and nested reviewer loops need explicit shape and stop criteria.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Workflow docs should name whether a loop is bounded, conditional, generate-and-check, fan-out-and-join, nested, or planner-executor, and should state the verified stop condition.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Potential ingest target: research-plan-implement-review lifecycle, subagent coordination, and AI-assisted TDD.

qualifying_updates.title: Cursor users ask for global AGENTS.md support across harnesses
qualifying_updates.summary: A Cursor feature request gained fresh July 20 comments asking for support for a global AGENTS.md path so multiple agent harnesses can share one durable instruction source.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: The practice issue is instruction provenance and scope: user-level, organization-level, and repository-level instructions need predictable precedence and update control.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Shared instruction files should have explicit scope, precedence, ownership, refresh expectations, and collision behavior across agent harnesses.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Use as a durable-instruction scope example, not a Cursor feature-tracking leaf.

qualifying_updates.title: Cursor community project packages specialized software-development roles as an MCP server
qualifying_updates.summary: A Cursor community showcase describes Software Factory MCP, an open-source MCP server that exposes specialized development roles including product manager, architect, backend, frontend, database, AI, QA, security, DevOps, code reviewer, and documentation writer.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: It reflects a local-practice trend toward packaging team roles and workflow contracts as callable tools or agents rather than relying on one general-purpose assistant.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Role-packaged agents need explicit task boundaries, handoff contracts, evidence requirements, and review gates before being treated as a software-development team.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Route broad MCP-server catalog coverage upstream; keep local note to subagent coordination and agent operating models.

qualifying_updates.title: Cursor confirms subagentStart deny hook report is reproducible
qualifying_updates.summary: A Cursor staff reply says they reproduced a report where a subagentStart hook returning deny appeared not to block the subagent, and suggested trying a preToolUse hook as a workaround.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: This is a concrete approval-control lesson: a UI denial or hook callback is not a governance boundary unless enforcement is tested at the actual execution point.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Permission hooks should be covered by regression tests that prove denied actions cannot proceed, including subagent launch paths and tool-use fallbacks.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Potential ingest target: destructive-command controls, human-agent approval boundaries, and tool-call governance.

qualifying_updates.title: Cursor subagent model reports expose cost and admin-policy drift
qualifying_updates.summary: A Cursor report says subagents can select more expensive models than the user configured, while a separate Enterprise report says the CLI listed an admin-blocked model as available and current before rejecting it at run time.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Agent-cost controls and model access controls need to align across UI, CLI catalogs, inherited subagent settings, and backend enforcement.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Cost and model governance should validate inherited subagent defaults, catalog visibility, configured policy, and runtime rejection paths as one contract.

qualifying_updates.title: Shell-command approval discussion asks for explainable command review
qualifying_updates.summary: A Cursor approval-flow discussion received a July 20 comment that side chat helps explain proposed commands, but a first-class Explain action in the approval card would be smoother.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Human approval quality depends on the reviewer understanding exact command strings, chained operations, arguments, expected effects, and failure modes before execution.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Approval UIs should present structured explanations for proposed commands and risky patterns in the same flow where the user grants permission.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Fold into approval-boundary and user-visible progress guidance during ingest.

qualifying_updates.title: Resource2Skill article frames multimodal resources as provenance-bearing agent skills
qualifying_updates.summary: Developers Digest summarizes Resource2Skill as a research-backed pattern for distilling tutorials, repositories, articles, code, and reference artifacts into executable agent skills while preserving source evidence.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: It extends durable instruction practice from hand-written SKILL.md files toward generated, reviewable, provenance-bearing workflow artifacts.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Generated agent skills should carry source provenance, license checks, human review, sandbox probes, and periodic revalidation before production use.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: During ingest, avoid broad paper coverage; focus on source-faithful skill distillation and validation practice.

qualifying_updates.title: McKinsey cost-management article recommends limits on retries, tool calls, and loops
qualifying_updates.summary: McKinsey recommends managing AI demand through outcome-oriented cost controls, including structured outputs, response-length caps, and limits on retries, tool calls, agent loops, and escalation paths.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: The operating-model pages should connect agent loop design and context usage to enterprise cost governance, not only developer productivity.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Agent adoption playbooks should include per-use-case budgets, loop and retry ceilings, structured-output constraints, and escalation policies tied to business value.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Potential ingest target: agent-cost telemetry and workflow-before-model-selection.
